messages:
maria: apiserver 503s in ap-south1 starting ~1765004970. saw SNAT exhaustion on proxy nodes, controller-manager restarts, GPU attach queue growing. anyone oncall?
omar: same, seeing lots of TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED. apiserver logs: `net/http: write tcp 10.0.12.34:443->10.0.78.90:52344: write: connection reset by peer`
sre-oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert P1234 triggered (oncall: @omar)
kai: did infra run a NAT pool change during the maintenance window? cloud-team rolled a NAT update at 1765004800.
anita: pushed conntrack bump to 200k on proxy nodes: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and enabled `tcp_tw_reuse=1`. also raised `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait` temporarily.
omar: metrics: apiserver QPS spike from hosted-llm (inference traffic) 2k -> 9.2k, 95th latency doubled. gpu-provisioner attach timeouts rising -> controller-manager leader election jitter and restarts.
lucy: suggestion: shed non-prod inference traffic to dedicated fallback pool or apply ingress rate-limits. spinning an extra small GPU pool is possible but costy (~+$5k/day) until we stabilize.
maria: temp mitigation plan: 1) add secondary IPs to proxy NICs to increase SNAT port space (rolling), 2) bump conntrack & tcp_tw_reuse on all proxies, 3) deploy ingress rate-limit for non-prod routes, 4) create alert for attach latency >30s. executing step 1 now.
omar: watching dashboards (conntrack usage, SNAT ports, apiserver QPS, controller-manager leader changes). if SNAT util >75% we will redirect non-prod to eu-north fallback.
maria: rolling IP add completed on 3/6 proxies, SNAT utilization dropped from 92% -> 45% on those nodes. overall cluster SNAT now trending down.
lucy: nice, please open a short postmortem with cost tradeoffs and a follow-up to increase permanent SNAT capacity or use NAT64-style autoscaling.
maria: will do. updating runbook and notifying cloud-team.
sre-oncall-bot: Incident P1234 marked RESOLVED at 1765005090 (probable root cause: SNAT pool exhaustion combined with a short burst of high fanout requests from hosted inference; secondary factors: controller-manager sensitivity to attach timeouts).
